p: Plenty of visitors zip in off the M62, spend the day inside Xscape and zip straight back out again, which is a shame, because Castleford has more to it than its motorway junction. It's the town where the sculptor Henry Moore was born, and its striking zigzag footbridge across the River Aire, opened in 2008, is worth a look if you head into the centre.

If you fancy some fresh air between activities, RSPB Fairburn Ings is only a few miles away. It's a nature reserve built on old mining land, with easy trails, hides and a good chance of spotting wildfowl on the lakes. Families with younger children will find the paths manageable, and it's a lovely contrast to the noise and lights of a big leisure centre.

Back at Xscape, a little planning goes a long way. Decide in advance which activities you're definitely doing and book them, then treat everything else as a bonus. Teenagers often prefer to be let loose with a budget and a meeting time, while younger kids are happiest with one big activity, a meal and a bit of time in the arcade-style games area.
If you're travelling a fair distance, Leeds is only around a twenty-minute drive away and Wakefield is closer still, so you can easily turn a visit into a weekend with a night in either city.

Busy times are, as you'd expect, Saturdays and school holidays. A weekday visit in term time is far calmer if you've got the option, and the car park is easier too. Whenever you go, keep a bag with snacks, drinks and a spare layer handy, as hopping between the snow slope and warm indoor venues can leave everyone flagging.
